slides.0.title: The Five Major White Grape Varieties
slides.0.subtitle: Level 1 · Module 2 · Lesson 2
slides.1.title: Five Key White Varieties
slides.1.points.0: 🍋 Chardonnay: 17% of all plantings — Australia's most widely planted variety. Clare, Margaret River, Yarra lead
slides.1.points.1: 🍈 Riesling: star of Clare Valley and Eden Valley; Australia's finest dry Riesling tradition
slides.1.points.2: 🥂 Sauvignon Blanc: Margaret River 'SBS' (Sémillon-Sauvignon Blanc) world-famous blend
slides.1.points.3: 🍊 Sémillon: Hunter Valley's secret weapon — ages magnificently for 15–20 years
slides.1.points.4: 🌿 Pinot Gris / Grigio: rising star in cool regions — Adelaide Hills, Mornington Peninsula
slides.2.title: Chardonnay: The Style Revolution
slides.2.points.0: 1980s style: 'butter bomb' — full malolactic, heavy new American oak (100%), rich and tropical
slides.2.points.1: 2000s shift: 'New Wave' Chardonnay — no or low new oak, no or partial malolactic, higher acidity
slides.2.points.2: Top examples: Giaconda (Beechworth), Leeuwin Estate Art Series (MR), Bass Phillip (Gippsland)
slides.2.points.3: Modern style: citrus, white peach, mineral — resembles white Burgundy
slides.3.title: Hunter Valley Sémillon: A Unique Treasure
slides.3.points.0: Harvested very early (January/February) — low alcohol (10–11%), high acid, bone dry
slides.3.points.1: Young (0–5 years): almost neutral — citrus, herb, green apple
slides.3.points.2: Aged (8–15 years): honey, toast, lanolin, beeswax — complex and rich
slides.3.points.3: No oak ageing needed — one of the world's most distinctive wine styles
slides.4.question: Hunter Valley Sémillon is harvested early at low alcohol. What does it develop after 8–15 years of ageing?
slides.4.options.1: Honey, toast, lanolin and beeswax — remarkable complexity without oak
slides.4.options.2: Heavy vanilla and coconut from oak
slides.4.explanation: Hunter Valley Sémillon starts out almost neutral when young but undergoes a magical transformation with age. After 8–15 years in bottle, it develops honey, toast, lanolin and beeswax complexity — all without oak contact. This bottle-aged evolution is one of Australia's most unique wine traditions.
slides.5.title: Lesson Summary
slides.5.points.0: Five key whites: Chardonnay (most planted), Riesling (Clare/Eden), Sauvignon Blanc (Margaret River), Sémillon (Hunter), Pinot Gris (cool regions)
slides.5.points.1: Australian Chardonnay has shifted from butter bomb to leaner, more mineral styles
slides.5.points.2: Hunter Sémillon is one of Australia's most distinctive wines — low alcohol, no oak, ages brilliantly
